subject: CareAtlas — Clarify PHI segmentation & evidence samples for BAA scope
messages:
From: Catherine Moore <catherine.moore@careatlas.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: legalops@careatlas.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify PHI segmentation and evidence samples for BAA scope

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. We’re finalizing our vendor selection workbook and need a few clarifications before we can complete our BAA scoping exercise. High level: CareAtlas will send patient identifiers and clinician notes through your ingestion endpoint in two different flows — a bulk batch transfer and a realtime transcription webhook. We need to confirm what counts as PHI in each flow and what evidence you can provide for segregation controls.

Specific asks (spread across the attached DPIA questions sheet):
- Can you confirm whether: (a) hosted API (shared tenancy) can be covered under your standard BAA or you require Dedicated/Private for PHI ingress?
- What controls are in place to ensure PHI sent in the realtime transcription webhook is not cached beyond ephemeral KV caches? We need retention guarantees and evidence (config/sample audit entries).
- For batch SFTP transfers, can you provide a redacted sample of audit logs showing file ingest, processing, and deletion timestamps?
- Do you support customer-side tokenization/pseudonymization hooks (pre-ingest) we can deploy if we opt to keep raw identifiers out of your environment?

We attached a short DPIA question list (careatlas_dpia_questions.xlsx) and sketched expected dataflows. LegalOps is on copy for BAA language mapping.

We'd like to get this resolved before our security review on 21 Jun. Can you (a) confirm feasibility and (b) indicate an ETA for sample artifacts?

—Catherine
Catherine Moore
Head of InfoSec, CareAtlas
(c) +1 415-555-0199
(attachment: careatlas_dpia_questions.xlsx)

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Catherine Moore <catherine.moore@careatlas.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify PHI segmentation and evidence samples for BAA scope

Catherine — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Priyom (product/security) and Laura (customer success/ onboarding) so we can answer from the three lenses you called out.

Quick summary answers up front:
1) Hosted API vs Dedicated/Private: We can support PHI on our hosted environment under a standard BAA in limited cases if the customer agrees to certain configuration guardrails (explicit retention periods, tenant pinning for model variants, and mandatory KV cache TTLs). For higher-assurance environments or where customers require physical isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private. We’ll outline the exact configuration required.

2) Realtime transcription caching/retention: The runtime uses ephemeral KV caches by default; we can enforce a zero-persistence policy for transcription streams and disable disk-backed caches for a tenant under a BAA. We will provide a sample audit-log extract (redacted) demonstrating ephemeral cache lifecycle (see attached).

3) Batch SFTP ingest: We support SFTP ingestion to a per-customer transient staging bucket; retention policies are configurable and deletions emit audit events. We can generate a redacted sample audit log with the events you requested (ingest -> processing -> deletion).

4) Tokenization/pseudonymization hooks: We support client-side tokenization helpers and offer a pre-ingest transform hook for customers that want to remove identifiers before they reach our environment. Workflows include deterministic mapping keys you can hold.

Next steps:
- Priyom will confirm the exact retention TTLs and prepare the redacted audit_log_sample.
- Laura will schedule a 30-min call with your technical ops to walk the dataflow and any required config.
- I will prepare a short note describing when Dedicated/Private is required vs hosted-with-guardrails.

ETA: We can share the redacted log + dataflow diagram by EOD Thursday (14 Jun). If that works, Laura — can you propose times for a call?

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_dataflow_v2.drawio)

From: Catherine Moore <catherine.moore@careatlas.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: legalops@careatlas.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 15:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify PHI segmentation and evidence samples for BAA scope

Diego / team —

Appreciate the rapid response. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Our security team prefers Dedicated for anything that includes direct patient identifiers, but they said they could accept hosted if we get concrete evidence and configuration controls showing tenant-level isolation and non-persistent transcription handling.
- For tokenization: we’d like examples of deterministic mapping approach (how you recommend handling lookup keys and rotation) so our engineering team can validate they can integrate it into the pre-ingest pipeline.
- For the audit logs, please redact patient identifiers but keep event-level detail and timestamps. Timestamp fidelity is important (millisecond resolution preferred).

LegalOps also flagged a request: please include a short attestation that log samples are production-derived (not synthetic), and the timeframe covered by the sample. If you cannot provide production-derived artifacts, notify us and we’ll accept a synthetic reproduction with steps to reproduce.

Call windows: Thu 14 Jun between 09:00–12:00 PT or 16:00–18:00 PT work for us.

—Catherine

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Catherine Moore <catherine.moore@careatlas.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify PHI segmentation and evidence samples for BAA scope

Hi Catherine — quick follow-up from our side. We prepared an initial package and attached three artifacts: (1) redacted audit_log_sample_redacted.csv (production-derived; window: 2028-05-01T00:00:00Z — 2028-05-07T23:59:59Z), (2) redwood_dataflow_v2.drawio (annotated with tenant-isolation callouts), and (3) a short note on tokenization best-practices (inline below).

Tokenization recommendations (summary):
- Deterministic pseudonymization using HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-rotated key stored in your KMS. This allows joinability while keeping identifiers opaque in our environment.
- Key rotation cadence: 30–90 days recommended; maintain a short key history for lookups during rotation windows.
- For transcription streams, we recommend applying tokenization at the agent side before sending audio/text; if you need low-latency de-tokenization for clinician workflows, set up a secure lookup service under your control.

Attestation: redwood.ai confirms the attached audit_log_sample_redacted.csv is derived from production logs with PHI values irreversibly redacted. The sample retains millisecond timestamps and event identifiers. If you need a notarized attestation, we can provide a signed statement via our legal team (allow 3–5 business days).

We’ll upload the artifacts to the Drive link and send an invite to your engineers ASAP. Laura will follow up to book the 30-min call in the windows you provided.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
